title: Cetaceans in West Africa: A Review of Species Present, Records and Conservation Challenges
content:
ABSTRACT

The marine and estuarine waters of West Africa host tens of cetacean species. There are many threats affecting cetaceans in the region, including bycatch, deliberate capture, habitat degradation, pollution and noise. To date, few dedicated cetacean studies have been conducted in the region, and a lack of baseline knowledge for many countries and species hinders effective conservation efforts. To partially address this gap, this review collated all known records of cetacean presence from Mauritania to Nigeria. Seventy-three sources were reviewed, and records of 34 species were found—nine mysticetes and 25 odontocetes. Various record types, including strandings, sightings and boat surveys, were evaluated, with strandings and sightings being the most common. Records reviewed here are likely under-representative, reflecting varying research effort by country. Although the results of this review indicate that more information is available than 15 years ago, there is still a need to conduct more systematic research to inform conservation efforts. Employing technologies that are currently under-utilised in the region, such as passive acoustic monitoring, will be valuable in future research. Finally, there is a need to provide resourcing for African researchers to pursue cetacean science, to raise awareness of cetacean conservation and reduce pressures on cetaceans.
